Self-formatting values

Source: R/val.R
val.Rd

val_num(), val_pct(), val_sci() and val_p() return a self-formatting value (rule 3.12): the number given, with the class weft_val put before its own classes, and a format that prints it as the function of the same name in fmt_num() and its siblings would. The value stays a number: it compares, sorts and plots as one. Only the way it turns into text changes, so one statement of the digits serves every sink: prose, a weft() string, paste(), glue::glue(), a plot title, a table and the console.

Usage

val_num(
  x,
  digits = NULL,
  sigfig = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  unit_form = NULL,
  plus = FALSE
)

val_pct(x, digits = NULL, sigfig = NULL, unit = NULL, plus = FALSE)

val_sci(x, digits = NULL, sigfig = NULL, unit = NULL, unit_form = NULL)

val_p(x, digits = NULL, label = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
as.character(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
format(x, target = "plain", ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
knit_print(x, options = NULL, inline = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
cli_format(x, style = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  nm = deparse1(substitute(x))
)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
x[...]

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
x[[...]]

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
x[...] <- value

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
x[[...]] <- value

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
c(...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
rep(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
unique(x, incomparables = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
xtfrm(x)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
as.list(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
Ops(e1, e2)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
chooseOpsMethod(x, y, mx, my, cl, reverse)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
Math(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
Summary(..., na.rm = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
mean(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
median(x, na.rm = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'weft_val'
drop_units(x)

Arguments

x

A number, a quantity, or a self-formatting value.

digits, sigfig, unit, unit_form, plus, label

As for fmt_num(), fmt_pct(), fmt_sci() and fmt_p().

...

Passed on, or ignored where the text says so.

target

"plain" (the default), "markdown", "tex", "ansi" (which is plain), "html" or "marquee". The last two give what the matching fmt_*() call gives for the same number and format; the html form has class c("html", "character") and the attribute html = TRUE.

options

Passed by knitr.

inline

For knit_print(): TRUE for inline R.

style

Not used (for cli_format()).

row.names, optional, nm

As for as.data.frame().

value

The new elements: numbers, or values of the same format.

incomparables

As for unique().

e1, e2

Operands.

y, mx, my, cl, reverse

As for chooseOpsMethod().

na.rm

As for Summary and median().

Value

A self-formatting value: the number, of class weft_val and its own classes.

Details

The constructors take the arguments of the formatter of the same name, except target and the collapse arguments, and refuse what it refuses with the same error, naming the function called. x is a double, an integer, an integer64, a weft_year, a units quantity (see u()) or a self-formatting value, whose number is then given the new format; anything else is a weft_construct_error. An element that is NA, NaN, Inf or -Inf is kept and not formatted: its text is NA, "NaN", "Inf" or "-Inf".

The texts are made when the value is made, under the configuration a formatter would use there (the knit's, or the working directory's _weft.yml): the markdown, the plain text read from it (rule 1.4.24) and the TeX form. A value made in one project keeps its texts after setwd(). A ladder of units (unit = "m|km") picks one rung for the whole vector, and v[1] keeps it. A value made with the default digits that prints a number that is not zero as zero is warned about once, then: a warned check of kind "printed as zero" in a knit, a weft_zero_warning outside one. Printing it never warns again.

What it gives. as.character(), format(), paste(), toString(), sprintf("%s", ), glue::glue(), message(), warning(), stop(), cli's {v} and {.val {v}}, a ggplot2 title or label, a printed data frame and knitr::kable() give the plain text. format(v, target = ) takes "plain" (the default), "markdown", "tex", "ansi" (plain), "html" or "marquee" (what the matching fmt_*() call gives); other arguments of format() are ignored. knitr::knit_print() gives the markdown, joined by ", " inline and one element per line otherwise, so a document with no weft hooks prints the value right in prose. print() writes a header naming the format, then the plain texts. Three limits are R's: cat() prints the number underneath (as it prints a Date), writeLines() refuses the value, and a for loop reads the numbers; give the first two format(v). sprintf("%.2f", v) formats the number, as asked.

Vectors. [, [[, rev(), rep(), head(), tail(), sort(), unique() and as.list() keep the format and the texts of the elements they keep. c() and [<- make the texts again for the whole result, under the configuration in force then; numbers given to them take the format. Values whose formats differ, or a value and anything that is not a number, do not combine: a weft_construct_error. c(3, v) is a plain number, because R dispatches c() on its first argument. When vctrs is loaded, vctrs::vec_c() and the dplyr verbs follow the same rules, and a value combined with a plain number gives a plain number.

Arithmetic drops the format (rule 3.12.7): +, *, round(), sum() and the rest give the result for the number underneath: a double, or what the class underneath gives (a units quantity, a weft_year). min(), max(), range(), mean() and median(), whose result is on the scale of their input, keep the format. A comparison gives a logical, so claim() judges the number.

In weft's constructs (rule 3.12.8) the format is put together with what is written at the use: a key written there replaces the format's key of that name (digits and sigfig replace each other); a number class written there that differs from the format's replaces it, with all its keys; otherwise the format's class and keys apply. `r v` in prose prints the markdown, in math its TeX, and `v`{.val} prints its own format. The ledger records the value only where weft resolves it: making it, converting it to text and printing it record nothing. A self-formatting value is never a named value for the filter: weft_values_write() refuses it (E46). Phrase functions such as ci() use its number and ignore its format.

Examples

v <- val_num(3.14159, digits = 2)
paste("Mean", v)
#> [1] "Mean 3.14"
v > 3
#> [1] TRUE
format(val_sci(1.2e-4), target = "markdown")
#> [1] "1.2 × 10^−4^"
